title: Ingest safeguard fanout with correlation resolver and tenant signal alignment
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: multiple services and SDKs emit structured logs with inconsistent correlation fields (trace_id / request_id / tx / correlation). This causes duplicate events in downstream sinks, mis-joined traces in dashboards, and excessive storage in ELK/Loki. Current enrichers perform synchronous lookups which add 40-120ms p99 to ingest latency for high-cardinality tenants. Goal: insert an ingest-side 'safeguard' component that canonicalizes correlation identifiers, deduplicates fanout, and provides a weakly-consistent mapping service for id translation without increasing p99 latency beyond our SLOs.
decisions: Introduce an inline lightweight Correlation Resolver in the edge ingestion mesh that canonicalizes to a tenant-scoped canonical_id and attaches a provenance header for debugging.

Deduplication will be applied at fanout time via a deterministic event fingerprint (tenant + canonical_id + truncated-payload-hash) with a short TTL (5m) in a high-throughput in-memory store (Redis cluster with 1s replication lag expectations).
Avoid synchronous enrichment calls to external identity services by using an async background reconciler that backfills mappings and exposes a reconciliation lag metric.
Retention of raw id fields: retain original fields in the raw payload for auditability but tag normalized fields for downstream consumers to prefer.
Use a feature flag gated rollout and traffic-weighted canary in two regions before global rollout.
tasks: Design correlation resolver API and header contract (edge -> ingest-fanout)
Implement resolver microservice with Redis-backed mapping and local LRU cache
Add deterministic fingerprinting and dedupe lookup at fanout worker
Update SDK sidecar / ingress adapters to send ‘x-rw-canonical-id-proposed’ when present
Create reconciliation worker that consumes tombstones and ID-merge events to backfill mappings
Instrumentation: expose ingest p50/p95/p99, dedupe rate, mapping-miss-rate, reconciliation-lag
End-to-end tests: multi-tenant dedupe, id-rotation, eventual-consistency scenarios
Kubernetes deployment manifests, HPA rules, and chaos tests for Redis failures
acceptance_criteria: New ingest pipeline canonicalizes IDs for >95% of active tenants in canary traffic
Deduplication reduces downstream duplicate event rate by at least 60% in canary signals
Ingest p99 latency increase <= 10ms relative to baseline in canary (measured by edge -> write completion)
Mapping-miss-rate tracked and reconciler reduces misses to <1% within 10 minutes for steady-state traffic
Playbook for emergency disable (feature flag off) reverses behavior within 90s
Confluence design doc and GH PR with code review approved and merged
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged internal traffic (10% in primary region) — 3 days
Phase 1: 50% production traffic in primary region + synthetic load tests — 4 days
Phase 2: cross-region (primary + secondary) 25% traffic with read-only replica of mapping store — 3 days
Phase 3: full rollout with monitoring runbook and cleanup of legacy enrichers — 1 week after stability
metrics_dashboards: grafana:ingest_edge_latency - p50/p95/p99 edge-to-storage broken out by tenant tier
sentry:ingest-resolver-exceptions - capture resolver panics and timeouts
risk_mitigation: Risk: Redis cluster outage causing durable dedupe failures -> Mitigation: fallback to best-effort fingerprinting without writes and raise alert; fail open to avoid blocking ingest.
Risk: Mis-canonicalization causing inconsistent joins -> Mitigation: keep original ids in payload and add a debug provenance header; provide a rollback path via flag.
Risk: Increased operational cost from dedupe write amplification -> Mitigation: TTL tuning and sampling strategy for low-volume tenants
Risk: Cross-tenant collision in fingerprint -> Mitigation: include tenant namespace in fingerprint and use 128-bit hash truncated to 64 bits
